clue.text: Worthless instrument lacking finish and really hollow

indicators.note: lacking its finish means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trumpet is a brass instrument

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of the word really is scooped out, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive critic calls some musical instrument a worthless, hollow thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking finish' cuts the last T from TRUMPET, giving TRUMPE; 'hollow' empties 'really' to RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy rubbish of no value, so as an adjective it means worthless.

clue.text: Joint action in wood — worm turning

indicators.note: in means the worm goes inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: turning means the letters of worm twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A worm turning inside a piece of wood, as if in a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests carpentry, fitting the wood and worm; here it means shared. 'turning' scrambles the worm before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is cooperative effort by a group acting together.

clue.text: Unqualified pro's first to leave golf club

indicators.note: to leave says that letter departs from the club

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the golf pro

explanation.surface: A golf professional leaves the club with no qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means complete, absolute, without any qualification.

clue.text: Capone is in for it — twisting Uncle Sam, say

indicators.note: twisting means these letters are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Al Capone is in trouble, twisting America's government figure round his finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is a human figure standing for the United States, a typical embodiment.

clue.text: Sally is ready to take in East German

indicators.note: to take in means one word holds the other

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to eat
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally is ready to welcome an East German visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name; it is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty remark, and a riposte is a sharp reply.

clue.text: The practice of music for Richter etc?

definitions.meaning: musicians practise runs of notes up and down the keyboard as daily exercises
the Richter measure of earthquakes is one of many graded systems of measurement

explanation.surface: It seems to ask what the great pianist Sviatoslav Richter practised.
explanation.walkthrough: Richter looks like the pianist, which fits the musical first half; it is really the earthquake measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Graded runs of notes and graded measuring systems share this one word.

clue.text: Bent economist prayed for moral guidance

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked economist prays for moral guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' also suggests crooked, apt for the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that wrongdoing will not be rewarded, a piece of moral teaching.

clue.text: Look comfortable pinching head from snowman? That's abominable!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: pinching means the comfortable phrase grips a letter inside

parts.note: at home means comfortable and at ease

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snowman losing its head looks like the Abominable Snowman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snowman' and 'abominable' together evoke the Abominable Snowman, or yeti.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means hateful or disgusting, just as abominable does.

clue.text: Stop old lady displaying family tree

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
one's old lady is one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: Someone tells an elderly woman to stop showing off her genealogy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemma is a genealogical diagram showing descent, a pedigree.

clue.text: Put out note that's not new

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale
second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: Someone put out a note saying an item was second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse a fire or light is to extinguish it.

clue.text: Moving wine back in cellar

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: the back of the word cellar is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is shifting bottles of wine to the back of the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion, so it matches moving as an adjective.

clue.text: Man, for example, eating beef next door

indicators.note: eating means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: humankind is one example of a primate
beef comes from the ox

explanation.surface: A neighbour is spotted eating beef next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately adjacent, which is what next door describes.

clue.text: Choice of suit in merchandise for veterans

indicators.note: in places the suit choice inside the word for merchandise

parts.note: merchandise means goods, wares
H or S: a choice between hearts and spades, two card suits

explanation.surface: A shopper choosing a suit from the merchandise offered to veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clothing, but 'suit' is a card suit: H OR S, hearts or spades, sits inside WARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Warhorses are old campaigners, people long experienced in their field.

clue.text: Somewhere in Surrey on vacation, eating food from the deli?

indicators.note: on vacation means the word eating is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: ham is a cold meat sold at a delicatessen

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker somewhere in Surrey eats delicatessen food.
explanation.walkthrough: Egham is a town in Surrey, the county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a particular Surrey town, an example of somewhere in that county.

clue.text: See about unopened case

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a valise is a small suitcase

explanation.surface: A detective sees something about a case that has not been opened.
explanation.definitionFit: To see in the sense of understanding is to grasp or become aware of something.

clue.text: King's killer one caught out as well as leading author

indicators.note: leading means this piece comes at the front

parts.note: as well as means and

indicators.note: out means these letters are removed

parts.note: a regicide is the killer of a king
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A regicide is caught, and so is a leading writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes IC from REGICIDE, leaving REGIDE; 'leading' puts AND first.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French novelist who won the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Prom regularly attended by Sir Henry brought back popular vocal harmonization

indicators.note: brought back means the whole string is read backwards
regularly takes every other letter of the word Prom

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood founded the Proms concerts

explanation.surface: The Proms, attended by their founder Sir Henry, look back on popular vocal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every other letter of Prom, and 'brought back' reverses the whole string. The Proms are London's summer classical concert season.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a style of pop singing built on close group harmony.

clue.text: Carriage turning in one's path

indicators.note: turning means the letters swing round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A carriage turns in somebody's path.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'one's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage with two or four wheels.

clue.text: Fault found by a daughter like Mary Celeste?

indicators.note: found by means the fault is placed beside the other pieces

parts.note: a rift is a fault or crack

explanation.surface: A family flaw passed to a daughter, as mysterious as the Mary Celeste.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Celeste was a ship found abandoned and drifting in 1872.
explanation.definitionFit: The ghost ship was found floating unmanned, at the mercy of the currents.

clue.text: Organ used by noteworthy musician

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instrument played by a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument, matching the musician; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The thymus is a gland in the chest, an organ of the immune system.

clue.text: Opposition leader in Djibouti is entrusted with mission

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone sent is dispatched on an errand

explanation.surface: The leader of the opposition in Djibouti is given a diplomatic mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement, the act of opposing an official view.

clue.text: Biblical character called up to cross lake

indicators.note: to cross means the lake letter cuts across the inside
in a down entry, up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: hailed means called out to

explanation.surface: A Bible figure was summoned to cross a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for called (DELIAH), as this is a down entry; 'to cross' sets the lake letter across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah is the woman in the Book of Judges who betrayed Samson.

clue.text: Nanny taking care of girl the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nanny is looking after a girl badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny' looks like a noun but is a verb, to fuss over.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to pamper and overprotect them, just as to cosset is.

clue.text: Furthest from alpha male in old age ——retiring

indicators.note: in means the male letter goes inside
retiring means the word age withdraws, going backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An alpha male retiring in old age is as far as can be from alpha.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses only age; 'alpha male' is a red herring split across definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is as far as possible from the first.

clue.text: Pinning down finely cooked tuna

indicators.note: pinning means the jumbled letters hold another word fast inside them
cooked means the letters of finely are prepared afresh

parts.note: down means low, as in spirits

explanation.surface: A cook pins down tuna that has been finely prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges FINELY into YELFIN, and 'Pinning' holds LOW in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowfin is a large species of tuna fish.

clue.text: Don swaps piano for fine bed

indicators.note: swaps means one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An Oxford don trades his piano for a fine bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher; it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress used as a bed.

clue.text: Song with origins in Southern plantation involving religious activity

indicators.note: the origins of the words are their first letters

parts.note: a ritual is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: A song born on a Southern plantation, tied up with religious practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual is a religious folk song of African American origin.

clue.text: Angelic child posed, getting tips from Tiepolo

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cherub model posed for, and picked up tips from, the painter Tiepolo.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a winged infant figure, a cherub, common in Baroque painting.

clue.text: Words on last page you can read finally

parts.note: thee is an old form of you

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A reader reaches the last page and the closing words at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories traditionally close with these two words printed on the final page.

clue.text: Bashful girl heard people with reservations

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: bashful means shy, and Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy girl overhears people who have doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservations' suggests doubts; it means the land set aside for Native American nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American nation, many of whom live on reservations.
